app.title: OTTD Tools
app.subtitle: Consist, income & FIRS chain calculator for OpenTTD + Iron Horse + FIRS 5
consist.empty: Add engines and wagons from the catalogue
table.name: Name
route.title: Route income
route.productionHint: What the industry makes per economy month. 0 = not stated: the consist is then assumed to always find a full load.
route.waitForFullLoadHint: The full-load order: the consist leaves only when it is full, so its round trip carries the time the source needs to build the load up.
route.waitForFullLoadNeedsFlow: Needs the source output above: with no flow there is nothing to wait for.
firs.title: FIRS cargo chains
firs.hint: Click a node to inspect. Click background to reset.
combined.title: Route profitability
combined.needConsist: Build a consist first on the Consist tab
combined.assumptions: Loaded and empty legs at their own steady speeds (the empty train runs lighter and faster), dwell time for loading and unloading included, no inflation (Iron Horse is incompatible with inflation).
opt.title: Best train for the job
opt.goalNeedsProduction: Ranking by haul needs the industry output — set Production above.
opt.maxTrainsHint: Upper bound on identical trains sharing the route; it applies under both goals. The search sweeps from one train up to the bound: a shorter interval lifts the station rating, so more trains not only haul more but can also earn more.
opt.productionHint: Industry output per economy month; 0 means the train is always filled to station length.
opt.fleetHint: Identical trains sharing the route. Every money figure in the row covers the whole fleet, and what the station hands over is shared by it.
opt.intervalHint: Days between train visits: the round trip divided by the number of trains. Rating thresholds are {thresholds} days.
opt.cargoTripHint: What the train finds waiting when it arrives: the share of the output the station received since its last visit, shared by the fleet and capped by the consist capacity — the figure after the slash. A longer round trip means a fuller train.
opt.fleetLimited: Not enough trains for what the station hands over: the figure is what this fleet can move.
opt.branchWait: Full-load order helps here: the consist stands {days} days building its load up, then leaves full. Without the order it would call every {interval} days with {cargo} on board and end up worse off.
opt.branchNoWait: Full-load order gets in the way here: standing for a full load would space the calls out to every {interval} days for {cargo} a trip, dropping the station rating and costing the route part of its haul. The figures are for a consist that leaves with whatever accumulated.
opt.ratingHint: Share of the output that reaches the station at this interval — the game's station rating formula (new train, no statue in town, manual cargo distribution). It is that share the fleet loads and earns on; money in the table covers the whole fleet.
opt.introLatest: Introduction dates are randomised — may appear only by
opt.introLegend: the vehicle may not be in the buy list yet: the game introduces it on an exact date (not on 1 January), and randomises that date forward by up to 1.5 years.
opt.introLegendExact: the vehicle may not be in the buy list yet: the game introduces it on an exact date, not on 1 January.
opt.assumptionProduction: One-way haul, empty return at own speed, what the station receives shared by the fleet, money for the whole fleet, no inflation. The Route income tab settles the same route the same way but costs a single train, so its figures differ where a row runs a fleet.
opt.assumption: One-way haul, empty return at own speed, train filled to station length, no inflation.
settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Named exactly as in the game's Advanced Settings — copy the values from your game so the numbers line up. Everything is stored in your browser.
settings.currencyHint: In-game exchange rates; calculations stay in pounds internally
settings.speedUnitHint: locale.units_velocity — whenever a speed is shown in the user interface, show it in the selected units
settings.freightTrainsHint: vehicle.freight_trains — multiplies cargo weight, so it changes speed on grades (default 1)
settings.slopeSteepnessHint: vehicle.train_slope_steepness — resistance added per tile on a hill (default 3)
settings.cargoAgingRateHint: economy.cargo_aging_rate — higher means payment drops off sooner (default 100)
settings.dayLengthHint: economy.day_length_factor (formerly «day length factor») — stretches economic periods, so a calendar year holds proportionally more trips and running cost
settings.inflationHint: Iron Horse throws a fatal GRF error with inflation enabled — keep off unless calculating vanilla
settings.capacityHint: Iron Horse GRF parameter for wagon capacity
settings.trackTypeHint: Used by the optimizer when picking vehicles
settings.hillTilesHint: How much of the train sits on the slope in the «on grade» figure
settings.priceYearHint: Only matters when inflation is on
settings.storageHint: Settings, the consist you built and route parameters are kept in localStorage.
settings.jgrppHint: Enable if you play JGRPP — adds the settings listed in the game under «Non-standard settings which are not in vanilla OpenTTD». Off means vanilla OpenTTD behaviour.
settings.vehicleCostsHint: difficulty.vehicle_costs — scales running costs of all vehicles
settings.subsidyMultiplierHint: difficulty.subsidy_multiplier — applied to income of subsidised cargo
settings.accelModelHint: vehicle.train_acceleration_model — realistic factors in weight, resistance and slopes; original ignores them
settings.gradualLoadingHint: order.gradual_loading — adds station dwell time to each trip (loading_speed units per 40 ticks)
settings.paymentAlgorithmHint: economy.payment_algorithm — Traditional caps transit time at 255 periods, so very slow hauls are not penalised further; Modern has no cap
settings.introRandomisationHint: vehicle.vehicle_intro_randomisation: the game shifts each vehicle's introduction date forward by a random 0…511 days, so a vehicle listed for a given year can turn up a year and a half later. Vanilla OpenTTD always does this; JGRPP lets you switch it off.
settings.costsWhenStoppedHint: difficulty.vehicle_costs_when_stopped — running costs are divided by this while the train is stopped (1 / N), so long station dwell gets cheaper
settings.inflationFixedDatesHint: economy.inflation_fixed_dates — only matters when inflation is on
settings.inflationWarnTitle: Iron Horse will not load with inflation on
settings.inflationGrfError: «Iron Horse is not compatible with OpenTTD Inflation. Please turn Inflation off in OpenTTD settings.»
settings.inflationWarnBody: The GRF throws this fatal error at load time, so this combination cannot occur in a real game. Keep inflation off unless you are calculating vanilla trains.
settings.inflationBanner: Inflation is on — Iron Horse refuses to load in that configuration, so these numbers do not match a real game.
settings.newgrfHint: Turn a set off to calculate with the game's default vehicles or cargos instead.
settings.ironHorseHint: Off — vanilla OpenTTD trains and wagons are used
settings.firsHint: Off — vanilla cargos and payment rates are used; the FIRS chains tab is hidden
settings.firsEconomyHint: Every economy has its own set of cargos and industries; it applies to all tabs at once
settings.timekeepingHint: economy.timekeeping_units — wallclock counts economic periods in real minutes instead of calendar years
settings.startingYearHint: game_creation.starting_year — the JGRPP inflation model "from the start date" counts its 170 years from here (default 1950)
settings.basecostHint: Purchase price multiplier (powers of two, as in the GRF's parameter list)
settings.basecostGrfHint: Enable if a base cost mod GRF is loaded. Such a GRF does not define vehicles, so OpenTTD applies its multipliers globally on top of the difficulty settings.
settings.basecostRunningHint: Running cost multiplier per running class. Iron Horse puts engines in the steam class and wagons in the diesel one; the electric class only shows up on vanilla electric engines.
settings.languageHint: Setting names follow the game's own translation, so they match your game
savegame.title: Import from a savegame
savegame.intro: Load a savegame and the calculator will show how the game's settings differ from yours. Nothing is applied until you confirm. The file is read in your browser and never leaves it.
savegame.identical: Your settings already match this game.
savegame.infoHint: These affect the game but have no model in the calculator, so they are not applied.
savegame.error.notASavegame: This is not an OpenTTD savegame.
savegame.error.tooOld: This savegame is version {version}; OpenTTD 12 and newer (savegame {minimum}) are supported.
savegame.error.broken: The savegame could not be read.
savegame.info.parametersUnknown: loaded; its parameters are not known to the calculator
